utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom, and in the interpreters' booth and the technical booth. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before I'll ask the usher to bring the witness in, I noticed that yesterday at the very end of the -- of our court hearing, there was some commotion on the side of the accused. If this would be anything that the Chamber should know about, of course there's an opportunity to bring it to our attention. If not, we'll just continue. Since I do not see any reaction at this very moment, I'd like to ask the usher to bring the witness in, but the usher has left the courtroom already. I assume that he's getting hold of the witness. Madam Registrar, may I just verify that the face and voice distortion are still effective at this moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Miss E.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in the courtroom again. May I remind you as I always say to witnesses that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you made yesterday. As I indicated to you yesterday, the cross-examination by Defence counsel will continue now. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, good morning again, and thank you for coming here again today. I'm going to continue my line of questioning. On the question of military equipment, you said that your father was a military, but that he did not have a rank. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you know that he was a simple soldier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, your father, did your father wear a uniform during the conflict, or at least part of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us what kind of uniform was your father wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally whatever uniform he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So he would put on in the morning the uniform he wore. But could you tell us what kind of uniform? Was it a camouflage uniform or were there different types of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mostly green.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did he also have a blue uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, according to you, as far as you know, have there been -- were there women that were members of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Could you tell us, what was approximately your height at the time of your incident, at the time of the accident approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: A metre and 20 centimetres perhaps, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to ask the application again of Rule 91.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, isn't it true to say that you said -- and I'm quoting from memory -- that at the time of the fact, your height was 1 metre 47?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I then said approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking you, did you say that you were 1 metre 47 centimetres tall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this correction. Now, Witness, so you were more like 150 rather than 120, do we agree on that? Could you perhaps give an audible answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned colleague is not referring to the evidence before this Trial Chamber, but rather a passage from the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I expected he did as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the way it has been presented is not entirely consistent with the way it appears in the statement. Therefore, I ask that the relevant words in the statement be put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please literally quote, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. I'm quoting the section that interests us, that's page 2 of the witness statement. "My mother tells me that when I was 9, I was about 147 centimetres tall," et cetera. The quote is this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you perhaps give us an answer? So were you taller than what you said a moment ago? Could you have been higher than what you said you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. That was ten years ago. I don't know exactly how tall I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, that was ten years ago, but could you confirm that your statement was given on the 27th of June, 2001, which is about nine months ago? Could you please give us an audible answer for the transcript, please. Could you please give an audible for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, you gave us an answer to a question yesterday, Prosecution question, in page 3072, line 4. And the question was the following: "Was there anyone else in the yard when you were hit at that moment in the yard, was there anyone else present?" Witness, at the time of that question, the first question, at the time of the incident, were you not also joined by another young child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was before the incident and not afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So -- very well. At that time, that child was no longer in the yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. But who was inside the house at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my house, there was my mother and another house below, a white house, in that house was my father's mother and my uncle's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In your house at the time, your father was not in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there other soldiers that were present either in the house or in the house below?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And during other days, on any other days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, your father, since he was a soldier, could you describe for us, if he had one, a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what that's called. I don't know anything about weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. But he did have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't keep it in the house. But if he had to go to the front line, then they would go to the HQ, and then they would take it. There was nothing in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for specifying this. Now, you said that your father went to the HQ. Where was this HQ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: First it was in Breka, Breka Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said beginning, so does this mean that the HQ changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they changed all the time. They didn't have a specific place. They would go from one set of premises to another. Whether they would be able to use one premises and then they would move to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this answer. You said that there were several different situations, different locations. But which organisation was this HQ? Was this brigade, was it a battalion, do you know which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, the premises that the HQ occupied to start with, where were they? Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went to the HQ. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for this answer. And your father, did he walk there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So we can deduce that the HQ was fairly close to where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't close.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is the distance, Witness, between the street that you just mentioned and the house where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not too far, but it is far. I don't know. Maybe five or six streets below. The HQ was more towards the city because we were really more in the suburbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said five or six streets. Do you have any idea of the distances? Do you think you could maybe give us an estimate in terms of distances, in terms of space? What was the distance from the HQ to your house? Would you be able to give us a distance, perhaps? If you cannot do, then you're not able to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this answer. But what is the distance between the spiky rock and your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because there was a round-about way, perhaps 2 or 3 kilometres, but as the crow flies, probably closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So the distance by road would have been 2 or 3 kilometres. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness -- I withdraw that. Witness, what is located below your house, underneath, I mean geologically speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, there was wood. But because there was great need for the firewood during the war, there was no longer wood. There was just like a rock. It wasn't really a valley. It wasn't a particularly high hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So there was a ridge or a crest behind your house -- below your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Witness, do you know who was on that ridge at the time during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to have the Rule 91 applied, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the experience I had yesterday with, when I followed your suggestion to apply Rule 91, was such that I will not apply again Rule 91 until it is clear to me as well that it should be applied. So please continue questioning and indicate the moment where you think that the contradiction is such that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. Well, all right, Mr. President. I would like to have the statement in Serbian shown, so perhaps she could read to us the beginning of the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you know, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we usually ask counsel to read the lines in the language they want to read it and not have the witnesses to read it themselves. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But may I show the statement to the witness to authenticate the signature, as we usually do, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Miss E, Mr. Piletta-Zanin has a document, and it will be shown to you now. Would you please tell us whether the signature which is on this document is yours. Yes, please, Mr. Usher, would you -- is it one page or more pages, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document has three pages in total, I believe. But the page -- the quote in question is only on one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please show it to the Prosecution. Please return it. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to read a quote. I believe this is a third paragraph of the statement that you gave, and this is -- the date is 27th of June, 2001. "The army defenders used to pass close by our house on their way to the front lines on the ridge above us." [Interpretation] End of quote. Thank you. Now, Witness, I just asked you what was on the little ridge which was above you, above your house, and you said in Serbian, Nista, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, do you think this is a good moment perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. If you want to continue to ask the witness exactly what she meant with her answer given in this courtroom and the answer given during her earlier statement, in order to clarify whether there is a good explanation for what might seem to be a contradiction, but not for certain is already a contradiction. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said in a written statement in June 2001 that the defenders of Sarajevo -- sorry, the Bosnian defenders had their front line a position on this little hill above your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not on that ridge. I think you misunderstood. Above that ridge there was a much higher hill, and this is where the front line was. But on that other place, it was just -- there was no -- there was just a Mahala, there were no soldiers, no trenches, there was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this precision. Now, this location, how far is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What location are you referring to, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Because the witness has now talked about the two places, the ridge she was mentioning during her testimony in Court here, and another place, the higher hill which might have been a ridge as well where the front line was. Would you please indicate which ridge you refer to in your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I'm referring to this other place mentioned by the witness. This is this higher hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How far was it from your house, Witness E?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly this. I said approximately. There was this Spicasta Stijena, the spiky rock that it was about 2 or 3 kilometres away, and the lines were right below so that I just don't know exactly. Believe me. I'm not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, I do not think that you are one. I merely want to know if on that hill above you, on the hill above your house, whether there was a front line. As you gave us the distance between this place and the first trenches, tell us how far were the front lines from your house? If you cannot do that, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I can't; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Witness, for this answer. Were there any trenches in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on that second ridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm referring to the area near your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it that you never saw trenches near your house during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, above the house there were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question was "near the house," not necessarily only above the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So you do not know if in that area there were any trenches. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will now quote from the same document. It is the same document, so I will circulate it once again, if you wish me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you read it, and if the Prosecution would please follow the source. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will do that. It is the third paragraph which reads: [In English] "The defenders' trenches were very close to the Serb trenches, within 50 to 100 metres of them." [Interpretation] This is the end of the quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking again if there were any trenches in the area. You told us that there were not, and yet on the 27th of June, you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, having regard to the wording of the question my friend is currently putting to the witness, I think it is required of him to read the next sentence in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please read the next sentence, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will come to it. That was my second question. On the last page, it said: [In English] "... From us would have been at least 700 metres air distance away."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's your question now, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you if there were any trenches in the area, and I believe you told me that that was not the case. And will you now answer this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: Around the house, there were none. But I repeat once again, we were not all that far from the front lines. We were not right next to them either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I noticed that you shifted from near the house to an area, which I understand as being the area near the house. You are now confronting the witness with a statement which says that "at least 700 metres away from the house." You are creating confusion, and I'll not allow you to continue creating confusion. Would you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Merely, we can look at the French transcript to see what I said exactly. I said several times "in the area" picking up the word that was used in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You started your questioning "near the house," Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you have an opportunity to see these trenches in the area under consideration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would just wait one second, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia will read exactly, at least in English, your questions in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: It's page 11, and it starts line 7: "Were there any trenches in the area?" Answer: "Do you mean on the second ridge?" Question: "I'm referring to the area near your house." Answer: "No, there were not." Question: "Witness, is it that you never saw trenches near your house during the war?" Answer: "No, as far as I know, above the house there were none." Question: "Witness, my question was near the house, not necessarily only above the house." Answer: "No." Question: "Very well. So you don't know if in the area there were any trenches. Is that so?" Answer: "No, as far as I know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It makes it quite clear, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Judge Nieto-Navia now spelled out in full detail what kind of confusion you create, and you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I'm grateful to the Chamber. I go back to my question about the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: These trenches which are 700 metres around the house, were they on front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trenches on which side of the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm referring to the trenches on the side of the army called the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, say the first trenches below, as you came out of the house, one could see them. And those others, no, who can see trenches? They wouldn't be called trenches if one could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That is an excellent question. But my question was whether these trenches were on the front line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the first trench, and I assume from your question that there was a system with several trenches in two depths. Is that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. How many trench lines were there between your house and the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten that, believe me, and I don't remember such minor details.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But we nevertheless agree that there were several rows of trenches between your house and the front line is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Miss E, may I --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ask you a question. When you refer to the trench, you could see any other trenches? You could not see the other trenches? You could not see where these trenches of the Bosnia-Herzegovinian army, or would they be trenches of the other army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that mean that they were a first line of trenches from the BiH army, and then a second line of trenches from the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the greatest of respect, the wording of the question doesn't allow for another possibility, if I could obliquely put it to you that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I could say this, Mr. President: To intimate my meaning, another purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not exactly understand what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I could refer you, Mr. President, back to the earlier scheduled incident that we heard evidence about involving two girls crossing the street, that particular trench could not be described as a front line trench, but it was a trench nevertheless for a different purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I let you continue the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That was precisely along the line of our questioning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, was your father engaged as a soldier to defend these trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are not sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure, yes. He went to the trenches. He participated in the defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, Witness, did these trenches serve also for the civilian movement, that is allowing them to move about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that there were several trenches, and I asked you if the civilians also could use these trenches to go from one point to another.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you yourself use these trenches to move about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to clarify, you spoke about different trenches. Did I understand you well, but is it correct that there were trenches in front of your house, never mind the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in front of my house but above our houses, there was another locality. There was another locality, and that locality was on the front line. And they had to use trenches in order to go and fetch water and things like that. But we didn't have to do that because we were slightly lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what is this locality that you just mentioned called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that locality above me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also called Sedrenik, except that it is higher up. It is at the beginning of Sedrenik and Spicasta Stijena, that locality is right underneath Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And therefore, Witness, I understand that your house is much further away from the spiky rock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not much, but it wasn't right beneath it; it was rather close by. But there were other houses above me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. The trenches that you mentioned a moment ago as those who were -- which were above your house, are they the ones that we're talking now about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is trench -- they were not big trenches. They were small. I mean, they were trenches made of sacks, of bags, so that the civilians could run by. And that was next to the houses which are below the Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we once again use a map which was already used by the Prosecution yesterday, a map showing -- a map showing the area under consideration. And so as to avoid any problems, perhaps the signature on the map should be somehow concealed, covered up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, talking about P3243?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe that it is a map, not very legible, but where the witness put some markings to indicate her house and something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I may remind both that the order that whatever is being shown on the ELMO should not be broadcasted out of this courtroom is still valid because it's not just a matter of the signature, but also of the location of the house. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what I mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise on the map that is to your right, do you recognise it as a map which represents the area in which you lived at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, will you please use the pointer to show where was your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, will you, to the best of your recollection, point at the front line at the time of your accident? Where were the front lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you keep it there so that we can clearly see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Will you once again move along the front line. If there is a front line, will you please point at that front line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, and with the President's leave, I want to ask you to mark this map. You will be given a black marker, and will you please draw this front line there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I ask the witness to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you will be given a black marker, and I will ask you to trace on the map the front line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the front line is not directly as I know it. It is only approximate because I can't read maps very well. So I'll try to help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Will you now point for us the trenches that you -- that we spoke about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you now please use a dotted line so that we can see the difference, and will you then trace the front line, of course, to the best of your recollection, needless to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, if I understood you well, there were several rows of trenches. Were there also some other rows of trenches which you know about and that you could know about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness. Witness, in relation to your incident at the time when you were struck, did you -- do you know if your incident was officially and duly reported to the administrative authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will consult with my colleague, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you use this also to inform the Chamber on how much time you'd still need for the cross-examination, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would like to do that, Mr. President, and I would like to show the witness a panorama photograph that may clarify the evidence in relation to various positions. That is, the evidence from cross-examination. With the leave of the Trial Chamber, I would seek to have that photograph shown to the witness. I used it during my opening. It is about 5 feet long, I should say 1 and a half metres long and I think about 20 centimetres wide. It would probably fit on the ledge behind the witness, and I would propose to ask the witness to identify her house. For that reason, perhaps it should be done in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we'll then move to closed session in order to make the protective measures effective. And I see there's already CS on my screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 10.05 a.m. -- On resuming at 10.36 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are now in open session again. Whatever orders there may have been of not broadcasting anything on the ELMO, this order is lifted as from now on. Madam Registrar, could you please help us with the documents tendered in evidence. I think some or even most of them will be under seal. All of them under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The enlarged photograph marked by the witness, P3657 under seal; the traumatology report in B/C/S, P1025 under seal; the English translation, P1025.1 under seal; the set of two photographs, P3273 under seal; the map marked by the witness, P3243 under seal; the 360-degree Quicktime movie, P3279Q under seal; and the video, P3280Q under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are all admitted into evidence, and the Defence will have an opportunity to check whether the photograph is exactly the same, apart from the wording. If this would be different, the Defence may inform the Chamber about it. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I merely wish to draw your attention to one fact, that with regard to the map which is P3243, we have no document. We do not have the source of origin; we do not know where this map comes from. We have no means of identifying various sites. It is not really very readable, and therefore I also note that it was admitted into evidence, but the Defence must say that it has -- that it encounters major difficulties in reading that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this map was attached to the statement made by the witness on the 27th of June, 2001. I therefore assume that my friend is saying that he would be grateful to know, or at least to have a copy of -- another copy of the map. Perhaps one that is more legible. I will make some inquiries, and if we have one, we will provide it to the Defence. Mr. President, whilst I'm on my feet, might I raise another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis will be taking the next two witnesses. Before that happens, might I return to the subject of medical consultations for General Galic. I raise that because if we are not sitting tomorrow, then we can inform the Victim Witness Unit accordingly so that some witnesses who are anxious to return may do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you'll allow me to confer with the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Registry has tried to get relevant information during the first break, and no final answer could be given yet by OLAT. During the next break we'll continue our efforts to find out exactly when the examination will take place and we'll inform the parties about it. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I did not hear Mr. Ierace answer the fundamental question, and that is whether there is a scale to this map. Can we know what is the scale of that map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'll take the lead on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I much appreciate it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During the examination of witnesses, distances which could be easily measured without asking the witness about the distances have been the subject of the examination. I order the parties to produce a map with a clear scale. And whenever the two points between which a distance might be of any relevance is not in dispute, so if the points are not in dispute, like as far as I see in this matter where we have the Spicasta Stijena and we have the location of a house, I'll allow no questions about what the distance as the crow flies is. Because we can measure it, we can compromise on it. There's no need to spend time on that during the examination of witnesses. Of course, if there's whatever specific reason to put into question the ability of a witness to estimate a distance, so if it's not the distance but the ability of a witness to estimate the distance, then of course the questions can be put to the witness. But if it's just about establishing the distance between two points, it is a bad system to ask a witness who is not prepared and who has not measured the distance to give us the information if there is far better information available. I hope that will save a lot of time. Then, Mr. Ierace, if the scale of the map is available, then we would like to be informed about it. And one of the problems about scales is as soon as you start copying, enlarging, or zooming in or zooming out, scale is not the same any more, unless you also copy the scale on the map. But I don't want to pay any attention to -- I would like to know about distances, but I'd like to have a proper way of establishing what a distance is. This brings me to the last observation I'll make before we continue with the examination of witnesses, is that as I told you before, this Chamber needs to have reliable information. A lot of military details of a person who is at that stage 10 years old might not be very Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. reliable. And since there are far better ways of finding out, it seems not very efficient to ask all these details to such a person where there are other persons who might know far better, where there are other sources which might give a far more precise indication, especially when we are using more time as indicated before. I think we could save time and avoid wasting time on this kind of questioning. Mr. Ierace, you are ready to examine your next witness? Mr. Mundis, the next witness will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prosecution calls Mejra Jusovic, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please bring in the witness, 11 Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since you are answering, I assume you can hear me in a language you understand by the translation. Could you please answer so that -- the microphone is quite at a distance. Perhaps the other two microphones are not in the direction of the witness and can be put on now again. Yes. Ms. Jusovic, before you testify in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence ask you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. And I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Ms. Jusovic. Ms. Jusovic, you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, the Prosecution who has called you as a witness, and you'll then be examined by counsel for the Defence, and if there are any additional questions by the Judges, we'll put them to you as well. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, Ms. Jusovic, can you please state your full name and provide your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Mejra Jusovic, born in 1948, resident of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, how long did you live in the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1964.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What area of Sarajevo or neighbourhood of Sarajevo do you live in?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I live in Stari Grad, old town, Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, when did the war begin in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: The war in Sarajevo began on the 6th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe for the Trial Chamber how your life changed as a result of the war's beginning.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: The change was big. We were left without electricity or water. We spent time in cellars. It was horrible. My husband was wounded in 1992 on the 12th of June. I had a son. He was also wounded twice. I was wounded in 1993, on the 24th, by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll discuss that in slightly greater detail in a few moments, Mrs. Jusovic. But first, I'd like to ask you whether Sedrenik, the area where you live -- where you lived -- was an area where sniping activities occurred?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware shortly after the war began that there were at least two major military forces that were competing for the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I take it from your testimony, though, you were aware that there was a war or an armed conflict that was occurring in Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I really did not know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've mentioned the area of Spicasta Stijena. Do you know what was or who was up on Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Whoever's position were there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the day that you were wounded by a sniper?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 24th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in which year was that, Mrs. Jusovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've testified that you didn't have any water or electricity once the war began. What did you have to do to obtain water?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We went at night. There was a cistern, a tank, and then we went at night to fetch the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did you use as a source of the heating and to cook, in light of the fact there was no electricity?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We went to a wood, to get some wood, also at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did this particular wood, where you went to collect firewood, have a name?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Pasino Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where was Pasino Brdo in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It is located above my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the time of late 1992, 1993, and into 1994, which government controlled the area where you were residing?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Probably Yugoslav, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention now to 24 July, 1993, the day you indicated that you were wounded by a sniper. Can you tell us what you were doing on that day, starting from the time when you woke up in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, I went at 3.00 a.m., I went to get the wood. And then at 6.00 a.m. when I returned, I was on my way back, I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On the day in question, were you with anyone or did you go by yourself to collect the firewood?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Tidza Papic was with me, and she went half an hour ahead of me, so when I was wounded, I was by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately, if you know, what time was it when you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Had the sun come up by that time?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was overcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how far the visibility was at 6.00 in the morning on the 24th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, it was overcast. You could see -- you could see that there was clouds, clouds moving, and that it was clearing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've testified that you were gathering wood that morning. Were you -- at the time you were shot, were you returning to your house?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And were you, in fact, carrying wood at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How were you carrying this wood? By what means were you carrying this wood?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I did not have any means. I was just carrying them on my back, on my shoulder, on my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you use a rope or some type of cord to tie the wood to carry it on your back?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had a rope, and we tied it. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how far from your house were you at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: About 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing any gunshots immediately prior to your being wounded?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Twice. There was a shot, and the third one hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you do when you heard the first and second gunshot?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I lay down on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: As you were walking towards your house on the morning that you were shot, what could you see in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: You could see a house, one house in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Farther off into the distance along the horizon, what geographic feature were you facing at the time you were walking to your house on that morning?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was turned towards Spicasta Stijena. I was facing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You just mentioned that you lay down on the ground once you heard the gunshots go off. Were you then --

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I lay on the ground, and I was facing Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you then struck by the third bullet?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where in your body were you hit by the bullet?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Left leg in the buttock.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What happened to you after you were struck by this bullet?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was on the ground for half an hour because I passed out, and then in the meantime, the neighbour informed my son. My son came, and they took me to the hospital. So I was not kept in the hospital. They took the bullet out, and then I was returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you have to go back to the hospital for any subsequent medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I went a couple of times to have a Band-aid changed. I went a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be shown the 360-degree Quicktime panorama photo which has been marked P3279R.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, I'd ask you to take a look at the screen in front of you. Do you recognise the view that is on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this picture is of? Can you please tell us what this photograph shows, please.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I can see my neighbour's house and the place where I was wounded. I can see Spicasta Stijena. You can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where in this photograph can you see Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: You can see Spicasta Stijena to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I assume, Mrs. Jusovic, that on the 24th of July, there was not snow on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, no there was no snow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, for the better understanding of the Chamber, could you please ask your technical assistant to move the cursor to where the witness might have located, just follow the ridge perhaps and then say stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I was intending on doing that, but first I want to get the witness to point out where his house is on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, is your house visible on the photograph in front of you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: You can see my house. You can see behind the big house, where you see the big house, and then to the left behind there is my house there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say "the big house," are you referring to the large house on the left-hand side of the photograph in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, yes. My house is just behind this house to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To the immediate right and below the big house is another house. Is that your house?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. My house is below this house which is big house on the left. You can see one house, but my house cannot be seen. You cannot see it from this big house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your house would be directly on the other side of the large house on the white photograph [sic]. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that would be slightly down the hill from the direction the photograph is facing.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, I'm going to ask that the photograph start moving slowly to the right. When you see Spicasta Stijena in the photograph, I would like you to say "stop."

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Stop. You've passed a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Is Spicasta Stijena visible in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for us where Spicasta Stijena is perhaps in relation to the house, the white house, in the middle and slightly to the left of the centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Spicasta Stijena is behind this white house, and it's to the left, in the left direction. And then over there, that's Pasino Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you referring -- when you refer to Spicasta Stijena, are you referring to the ridge towards the left of the photograph at the horizon which includes a number of trees?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, what's covered, that's Spicasta Stijena. What's covered with trees, that's Spicasta Stijena. To the left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the photograph be panned to the right, please. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, do you recognise the area that's now visible in the photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: All this is part of Pasino Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this would be the area where you would go to retrieve firewood to use for heating and cooking?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on the morning that you had been shot, this is the area that you had gathered the wood in prior to returning home. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the photo continue to be panned to the right, please. Thank you, you can pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, what was your intended route to return home --

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was your intended route to return home on the morning when you were shot? In other words, how would you have gotten from the point where this photo is taken to your house on that morning had you not been shot?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I was going down Pasino Brdo, and then I went to Rasadnjak, this garden area. This is the route I would have taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would you have then continued between the two white houses in the centre of the photograph, and then gone to the left to your house?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown the videotape which is marked P328R.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Would you please stand in the location where, to the best of your recollection, you were when you were wounded on the 24th of July, 1993. "Could you now please point in the direction where, to the best of your recollection, you heard the shot come from at the time you were wounded. "THE WITNESS ON TAPE: From up above, from the road. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you point in that direction please again and hold it for about 3 seconds. "THE WITNESS ON TAPE: From the rock. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, did you recognise yourself in that videotape?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, did you comply with the directions of the investigators truthfully?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, were there any other -- on any other occasions as you were returning from Pasino Brdo having collected firewood did you hear gunshots?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No. I only heard it from up there, from Spicasta Stijena. This is where the shots came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me try to rephrase my question. On any other occasion when you were coming down from Pasino Brdo did you hear gunshots from Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything until I came to cross that pit. And when I came to cross that, that's when the gunfire started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, may I ask you a question. I think Mr. Mundis was asking on whether a day before, a week before, a month before there was ever -- did you ever hear any fire coming from Spicasta Stijena? So not on that same day, but at any other occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, there was gunfire from up there every day, from Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, were there any other occasions when you were grazed or wounded or hit by a bullet, other than the 24th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall the date. I was going with Naza Ocuz, and I was not shot at. I was not shot but I was grazed. There was a fragmentation bullet that grazed me, and the bottom bit of my track suit had burned, burned away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, did people who lived in your area in Sedrenik take any type of protective measures with respect to these snipers, to protect their homes or their property from snipers? Did you do anything?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we put concrete slabs on our windows. Then we put up blankets. But none of this really had any effect because we were in our cellars. If you try to get out, then they would shoot at you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During 1993, approximately on an average day, approximately how many hours would you stay in your basement?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: We would spend the entire day in the cellar. We could only move about during the night. If we needed anything like water or wood, it was only at night that we could move about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, did you become aware of other neighbours or people who lived in Sedrenik who were the victims of snipers?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Rasida Nedic, she was killed immediately. And then Salko Parla, he was also killed. And then there were many who I did not know. They were refugees. Ibro Coso also, he was killed by snipers. Many others wounded. Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've mentioned three people by name. Do you know the approximate date or year in which those people were killed?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was in 1993, but I couldn't tell you the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, I neglected to ask you earlier, on the day when you were grazed by the bullet when your trousers were damaged by the bullet, do you remember the approximate time frame that that was? Perhaps what year or month or season that grazing incident took place?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was in August, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions for the witness at this time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Ms. Pilipovic, you're on your feet. May I assume that you're ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mrs. Jusovic, questions will now be put to you by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Jusovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether in the period sometime during 2000 you spoke to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in 2001, yes, I did. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was this, if you remember, on the 4th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was this your first interview that you had with the representatives of the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before the 4th of May, 2001, and from the moment that the incident happened, the incident you told us about today, did you speak to any persons from the competent authorities, for instance, the police? Did you give a statement to the police because of what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: After the incident happened, the incident you told us about, did you report this incident to anyone except that you went to the Kosevo hospital to be treated? Did you report this incident to anyone that this incident had happened?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't report it to anyone. I was just taken to the hospital, and they took the bullet out in the hospital. I couldn't -- I couldn't -- I couldn't do that. I couldn't report it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that the incident you told us about -- and it was the very first time that you spoke to the Prosecutor's office representatives on the 4th of May, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us then, in 2001, when you gave your statement, what was your recollection like or memory in relation to when the incident happened? How fresh was your memory in relation to the time when the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you, the trauma remained with me. It is terrible. I'm telling you it's terrible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you gave the statement to the Prosecutor's office, did you have the statement read to you?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign that statement? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you confirm with your signature that what has been put in the statement, what you said yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm to us that on the 18th of February, 2002, you spoke to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you told us that you have been living in Sedrenik since 1964.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if a part of Sedrenik in which you lived has a street, and what is the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Sedrenik 133 B.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that you lived on Sedrenik Street -- what was the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: 133 B. Are there any other streets in Sedrenik called that, or is there only that street which is called Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It is the only such street as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us the street that you lived in? When I say "can you describe it," I mean can you tell us if it is a steep street that you have to climb down, or is it flat and it has no hills?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is a flat street, a level street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that there are no elevations or drops in that street?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. There are bends.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what does "bends" mean?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it bends, that the streets are not flat, but where I live it is flat or perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us your house, you say that it is flat, that it is straight. Does it mean that it is at the foot of the street or is the part of the street where you are, is this street which is flat in the upper part?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Well, my house is not exactly on the street itself; it is some way away from the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that your husband had been wounded in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe in more detail the situation and the location where your husband was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: My husband was wounded in the yard. That is, in the door, as he was coming out so that we could hide in the cellar because the shelling had started. Two shells had fallen there and the third one wounded him at the very entrance door.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us from which direction, if you can determine, did this shell come from?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was inside the house when the two shells fell. We were inside the house, and that was when we started for the cellar. So which position it came from, I really can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was in 1992 on the 24th of July, around 1.00 in the daytime.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You tell us it was in daytime, around 1.00. Can you tell us if that day there was any gunfire? I mean, was there any shelling and small-arms fire in the part that you live in?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: That day was quiet, and then out of the blue the shelling started.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You are telling us that it was on the 24th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence should like to show the witness a part of the statement she gave to the investigators of the OTP on the 4th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want to confront the witness with the date of the injuries her husband suffered? Would you then please, first, if you've got one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's right, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you asked, Ms. Pilipovic, about the day the husband of the witness was wounded, I was at that very moment to remind you that it was a repetitious question because it had been -- it was told before by the witness. She said: "My husband was wounded in 1992 on the 12th of June." So therefore, before you take her to her earlier statement, would you please verify whether the testimony where she says it was the 24th of July, which seems to be the day exactly the same as the day and the year, although one year earlier when she was wounded herself, whether there's any misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, like this. In line 22, 12.12, 24th of July, 1992. And then I ask her again if it was on the 24th of July, and here I see in the transcript "1993." I don't know why. Because all I wanted her to do was that was on the 24th of July, 1992. So that is the day about which the witness says that her husband was wounded on. And she tells us that it was 1992 when my learned friend asked her --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think you must be precise. Since my laptop did start late, it was not connected, I couldn't indicate the exact line to you. But it was one of the first questions. Could you please find where the question was put to her what area, neighbourhood in Sarajevo did you live in? That's right in the beginning of the examination-in-chief. The answer was "I live in Stari Grad, old town, Sedrenik." And the next question was about when the war began. And then what changed at the beginning of the war. And then upon this question on the changes, and I now read literally, part of the answer was: "It was horrible. My husband was wounded 1992 on the 12th of June." It was very precise. I mean it gives the date and the year. So perhaps before lose any more time, Mr. Mundis, you'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. President, that's page 44, lines 22 and 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just first clarify this. Mrs. Jusovic, when you were examined by Mr. Mundis, you told us that your husband was wounded on the 12th of June, 1992. When examined by Ms. Pilipovic, you gave another date, I think it was the 24th of July, 1992 as well. Yes. Could you tell us what was, if you still -- what was the date your husband was wounded? You gave two dates, and I would like to find out which was the correct one. We are not talking about you, about when your husband was wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is where I was wrong. My husband was wounded on the 12th of June, 1992. And I was wounded on the 24th of July. So this was the mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in 1993, and my husband was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when asked by my learned friend, you said that your son was wounded twice. I apologise, perhaps I did not hear you well or understand you well. I believe you said, "I had a son."

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was wounded twice. He was severely disabled, and I did not...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how old is your son?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: He was born in 1970.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where was your son wounded the first time?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: It was -- the first time it was a shell which wounded him near the house. And the second time, it was a sniper who struck him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the first time by a shell, when was that? When I say what year, I'm referring to 1992, 1993, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: He was wounded in 1992. 1992, on the 8th of October the first time by a shell. And then again by a sniper in 1992, too, on the 10th of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if your son was a member of the Territorial Defence of Sedrenik, subsequently the BH army? Did he participate in the defence?

utterances.speaker: MEJRA JUSOVIC
utterances.text: No, he did not participate anywhere because he was ill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Jusovic, I see that you are even a bit shaking. If you are nervous and if you need some extra time, please tell me so that we can arrange perhaps for a short break. We are anyhow at the moment where we should have a break. So if you think you need a quarter of an hour, 20 minutes, have a glass of water and recover a bit, because I see that it's rather emotional to you. You don't have to be ashamed for it. It's quite understandable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am distressed because of my son, because I didn't see my son for eight years, and I'm now reminded of it. I don't even know where I summon strength to come here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We're quite happy that you are here. We feel that it's not easy for you. Perhaps we are at a moment where we would have a break anyhow. Perhaps we'll have a break for just 15 to 20 minutes, and we'll then resume. And just upon returning in this courtroom, tell me whether you're able to continue to testify. Yes. Yes, please, Mr. Usher, would you first take care of the witness. We'll adjourn until 25 minutes to 1.00. --- Break taken at 12.15 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd first like to inform the Defence and the Prosecution that we have no confirmation yet as far as the time of the medical examination is concerned. I do understand that the normal procedure would be that the Defence keeps constantly in touch with OLAT, and as soon as we know whether it will be still today or tomorrow morning, especially if it would be tomorrow morning, that the Defence then immediately informs the Prosecution so that they can arrange for whatever they have to arrange. That's the first remark I'd like to make. The second one is that I'm informed that the witness is not able at this moment to continue to be cross-examined. She needs professional help at this very moment, and I do understand that she'll get it this afternoon. Without interfering in whatever way with the right of the Defence to cross-examine the witness, I would nevertheless ask you to consider whether you feel a need, even under the present circumstances, to continue the cross-examination. We'll have to be aware that when the witness is able to continue to be cross-examined, of course she'll be available. I do not know, of course, what you still had in mind to ask her. I have the experience that very often, you ask about military presence in the neighbourhood. On the basis of what the testimony was until this moment, I do not expect very detailed or clear answers to that, since the witness has testified that she thought she was still under the Yugoslavian government and she didn't know anything about parties in the war. Of course I'm not interfering in any way. Until now, I think the most important issue touched upon in cross-examination was the wounding of her husband and her son. I think that created the very emotional state that she is in now. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. If the Defence would consider that the continuation of the cross-examination is not of such importance for the Defence, that it would be necessary to continue, I'd like to know. Otherwise, I expect that the Defence wishes to continue the cross-examination. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
